newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil pension funds seen joining CSN consortium.
newsitem.headline: Brazil pension funds seen joining CSN consortium.

text.p: A group of Brazilian pension funds that intends to take part in the privatization auction of state mining giant CVRD is widely expected to join the consortium led by Brazilian steelmaker CSN to bid in the sell-off.
"There is a large possibility that the pension funds will join CSN," said CSN spokesman Francisco Padilha. "Nothing has been signed yet but we are in talks at the very moment."

The pension funds have been coveted by the CSN group as well as by a second consortium planning to participate in the April 29 auction of a 40-45 percent voting block in CVRD given their existing stake in CVRD.

The group of six pension funds - Previ, Petros, Sistel, Funcef, Fapes, Funcesp - has a joint 13.4-percent voting stake in CVRD which would give the winning consortium a controlling position in CVRD if the funds are on its side.
The block of pension funds had an even larger joint share of 15 percent of CVRD voting capital, but CVRD's own pension fund, Valia, decided to drop out of the group at the last minute.

Valia Superintendent Director Adir Pereira said Valia was teaming up instead with the employees of CVRD, who have the right to buy 4.45 percent of CVRD voting shares, to join after the auction whichever consortium emerges as the winner.

The other consortium in the running for CVRD, named Valecom, is led by Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim and South Africa's Anglo-American Corp, and is likely to also include Banco Safra and a group of 12 Japanese companies led by Nippon Steel.

Rodrigo Marques, analyst with investment bank Bozano, Simonsen, said the pension funds were more likely to team up with CSN than with Valecom because the CSN consortium would give the funds greater say in the administration of the CVRD stake.
"In Valecom, Votorantim and Anglo-American will be leading the way and the funds want a more active voice in the consortium," Marques said. "CSN plans to give its associates greater say."
The CSN consortium is based on a power sharing prinicple where all members of the group have an equal say in how to administer the CVRD stake.
Valecom plans to centralize power by making Votorantim Chief Executive Antonio Ermirio de Moraes chairman of the special purpose company which will run the 40-45 percent stake.

CSN is also looking to close a deal with pulp and paper firm Cia. Suzano, construction firm Camargo Correia, metal and metallurgical company Caemi, Nations Bank, Opportunity Asset Management and South Africa's Gencor.

Brazil's largest retail bank Bradesco, which is barred from participating directly in any consortium bidding for CVRD because it was one of the consultants on the CVRD sell-off, may participate indirectly in the CSN group, Padilha said.
Bradesco is looking to help finance the CSN bid by placing money in an investment fund specifically created to take part in the CSN consortium, he said.
